parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of what MarkTaskDoneUseCase.execute does fits the application layer. It loads the task through the TaskRepository port, calls the domain behaviour task.markDone(), saves the result and maps the entity to a TaskOutput DTO. The one problem is the error handling. The use case turns "not found" and TaskAlreadyDoneError into ApplicationError objects that carry the HTTP status codes 404 and 409. Choosing a transport status code is a presentation/transport (infrastructure) job: the controller in src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts or the HTTP server should translate errors into HTTP responses. With the codes chosen here, the application layer is tied to HTTP. A transport-neutral error kind (for example NotFound or Conflict) would keep this responsibility in the right place. This is a fairly small leak, so confidence is moderate.

violations.message: MarkTaskDoneUseCase.execute picks HTTP status codes (404 via `new ApplicationError("task not found", 404)` and 409 via `new ApplicationError(error.message, 409)`). Translating errors into HTTP status codes belongs to the transport layer (infrastructure, e.g. TaskController), not the application layer. The use case should raise transport-neutral error kinds instead.
